summary: @hubsync/web-sdk-react preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`, which downloads a Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts it, marks the binary executable, and invokes the shipped 727KB `math_init.js` via `execFileSync(bunBinary, [math_init.js])` at npm install time. `math_init.js` is a heavily obfuscated single-line bundle (obfuscator.io-style string-array rotation via `WV8StW` over the `n7gIxM` table, hex-mangled identifiers, `// @bun @bun-cjs` header) with no accompanying source, sourcemap, or build config. The package.json `description` field is 'Verdocs Web SDK for React' and README.md is a verbatim copy of the Verdocs React SDK README (including install instructions pointing at `@verdocs/web-sdk-react`), while this package is published under the unrelated `@hubsync` scope. A React UI SDK has no legitimate need for a separate Bun runtime; routing execution through a freshly downloaded alternate runtime causes the payload to bypass Node-based install-time inspection. The delivery pattern (unverified runtime fetch + install-time execution of an opaque bundle + publisher/README impersonation of another vendor's SDK) is an alternate-runtime dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
